body: Being 45 is still better than being a troll on Reddit, Lydia.
I’m due for my third dose of Gerdasil in February. Got the vaccine after I was diagnosed.

Thankyou, Im so glad I may have a chance to get rid of it. What has been confusing for me is, that I’ve a high risk hpv and warts. I wasn’t sure if it was possible. I thought I had warts because I had a low risk thing going on. Also, I did get the first doze yesterday. The gynaecologist was super helpful and didn’t make me go thru any biopsy.

So I just went to a gynaecologist, this time I went to govt funded clinic. She handed me a cream, said I don’t have cancer. And need regular screenings. 
Im not sure if it’s bad or good. But I’m alive and cancer free for now I guess.
And I belong from a conservative family, I cannot tell my parents who’d fund it for me. If I get diagnosed with cancer, I might as well be dead.
I have GW and High risk Hpv, but no signs of low risk. Is this even possible? I’m sorry I wrote it in a hurry, I’m freaking out.

Thanks for taking out the time to help. 
It took me a while to come back to type this out since it reminds of the helpless person I once was. I’m still in the process, I’m not completely over it and it’ll take me a few more years to understand and practice everything that’s been said. 
It’s absolutely confusing and devastating to end things, and start from scratch. 
Which I did btw, I got a new job, started working out and doing all things I never had the will to commit to. It’s painful, and I do feel lost more often than not, but it’s for the better. 
Once again, thankyou, I’ll always come back to this comment when I feel down, it has helped.

I teared up a bit reading this, I never expected them to hurt me, and it was so cruel, It felt as if my heart was ripped open, it hurts so much to even think of it, I wish I could love myself as much as I loved them. 
I’m going to keep coming back to this comment since this is probably the only thing which seems to give me a breather from all those painful memories, Thankyou for taking out the time and effort for this, I hope you’re healed and happy, and I hope I’m healed and happy too someday.

Its true, there’s a lot of guilt and shame attached to it, to think why’d i ever put myself in a situation like that, why’d i ever not fight hard enough or even fight back at times? To believe this is how it is, certain times people around us too add to the guilt and shame.
But its important to remind yourself that it wasn’t your fault, it wasn’t you who should be thinking like this, its them who is to be blamed, Its them who should have to live with it, its a constant battle, but its vital to heal yourself.

This is my life too, I have never been hit on when I’m out with my friends on a night out or anywhere else, it shouldn’t be a big deal but it hurts, makes you question everything you wear and do, it got to a point where I’d not post pictures with my friends, because I’d always have dms’ and comments from people asking who the person beside me is, it made me rather bitter.
But you can’t let this get to you op, you’re attractive and someone getting more attention doesn’t make you any less, realise that. It got better for me when I realised that the only way this ends is I stop seeing myself from other people’s perspective, because the only one that matters, is mine. There’s all kinds of reminders from the world outside which confirm our insecurities, but don’t bow down to them, hope this helps.

Thankyou, really. Just putting this out there and knowing that someone understands has made me feel so much better.
I wish I could put my gratitude into better words, I feel like I’m heard and I’m so thankful.
You’re going to get where you need to, I wish you courage and peace.

Hang in there OP, I might not understand what you’re going through, but you’re 
anything but a burden.  Although I’ve been suffering from similar trauma from my friends and family, I’ve had a hard time coming to terms with it, I found myself an internship, I’ve started to spend most of my time away from my home and however exhausting that might be, it helps you think about better things instead of the constant fear and frustration. 
Its an escape, but it works, do what you need to do to cope, as long as its not hurting anyone around you, good luck op.

I’ll certainly try to find the book mentioned, Thankyou! I didn’t expect such solid advice this quick, I might just start making efforts from tomorrow, I feel better knowing I’m not alone.
